newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dissident vows bush war if expelled from Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Dissident vows bush war if expelled from Kenya.

text.p: A Kenyan dissident politician said on Saturday he would try to enter Kenya once more after being refused entry earlier this month and vowed a guerrilla war on President Daniel arap Moi if he is turned away again.

Sheikh Khalid Balala, a radical Moslem preacher and a leading voice of dissent against Moi's government, told Reuters he was about to catch a plane to the Kenyan capital Nairobi to register by the July 1 deadline to stand in December elections.
"I want to go peacefully and seek democratic reform. There are signs and indications they will let me in this time," said Balala, speaking by telephone from Frankfurt airport.

"If they don't let me in this time and force me back to Germany, I will fly back by a secret route to the bush and wage an armed struggle against an oppressive regime similar to that (armed struggle) of (new Congo president Laurent) Kabila against (deposed president) Mobuto (Sese Seko)," Balala said.

Balala was refused entry to Kenya on June 7 when security officers detained him as he arrived at the coastal resort of Mombasa aboard an airliner from Frankfurt and forced him to return to Germany, where he has lived for the past two years.
He said his passport had expired while he was in Germany but the Kenyan embassy in Bonn refused to renew it. He said he had German travel documents but remained a Kenyan citizen.

Kenyan immigration officials have said Balala, who has a Kenyan mother and Yemeni father, automatically gave up his Kenyan citizenship when he failed to renounce his Yemeni citizenship at the age of 21.
President Moi, aged 73 and in power since 1978, must call elections in 1997 pitting the ruling KANU party against an opposition fractured mainly along ethnic and personal lines.
Balala's supporters in Kenya have said opposition groups would hold nine rallies across Kenya this month to press for minimum constitutional reforms before the elections.
